subject: Renewal + new workloads — post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@strideworks.com>, Tom Wheeler <twheeler@strideworks.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal + new workloads — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call and the proposed next steps so everyone is aligned. I tried to keep this short and actionable.

What we heard (pain points):
- Growing RAG workload for support search causing token cost to spike in Q2; prefix reuse is low due to truncated contexts.
- Need for predictable latency for the in-chat assistant during peak hours (SLO target 150ms p95).
- Procurement wants a clear cost model and timeline for Dedicated (reserved capacity) to evaluate budget impact.

Goals you shared:
- Stabilize inference unit cost while supporting a 3x increase in query volume by Nov.
- Pilot Dedicated capacity for two mid-sized models (embedding + chat) with canary rollout in production.
- Finalize procurement terms by end of September to align with budget cycle.

What we proposed (recap):
1) Pilot scope: Dedicated pool (2x A100 equiv) for chat + embeddings for Customer Support team — 6-week pilot including throughput tests and latency baselines.
2) Cost model: Attached draft cost model (redwood_cost-model-proposal-v2.xlsx) with 3 scenarios (on-demand, reserved, burst).
3) Technical checklist: We will run a short prefix-caching experiment and recommend KV-cache tweaks plus a tokenizer-level pre-batching config to lower per-token cost.

Immediate next steps (owners & timing):
- Sergio: Share Q2 usage export and Redwood pilot SLA exception request (today) — attached.
- Vanessa: Technical kickoff call with your infra lead to map network/VPC requirements (w/in 5 business days).
- Elena/Tom: Confirm procurement point-of-contact and high-level budget guardrails (by 2026-08-10).

Attachments referenced: strideworks_q2_usage_report.csv (attached), redwood_cost-model-proposal-v2.xlsx (attached), sla-exception-request.pdf (attached).

If anything above is incorrect or missing, please flag and I will update. If this looks good, Elena can reply with procurement contact and availability for a 30–45 minute technical kickoff next week.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Sergio — thanks for the clear summary. Quick confirmations and a couple of clarifications: 

Confirmations:
- The pain points and goals are accurate. The support assistant latency during our US West peak (11:00–14:00 PT) is the current blocker.
- Procurement timeline: yes, aiming to have commercial terms agreed by EoS Sept so finance can include it in the Oct budget.

Clarifications / asks:
- Can you include an estimated delta in monthly spend for the 3 scenarios in the spreadsheet (we need a hard number for budget planning)?
- For the pilot, can we include one longer-context model (8k) and one shorter (2k) so we measure both latency and cost tradeoffs?

Procurement contact: procurement@strideworks.com (I copied the alias above) — they’ll loop in our legal if we get to T&Cs.

Availability: We can do the technical kickoff next Wed 2026-08-11 at 10:00 PT — Tom and our infra lead (Marcus Lin) will join.

Elena
